title: Parent-Based Intervention for Childhood Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID)
official: Parent-Based Intervention for Childhood Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID)
summary: This study aims to test the efficacy of a parent-based approach to treating Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID) in children, SPACE-ARFID (Supportive Parenting for Anxious Childhood Emotions, adapted for ARFID), by comparing it to Nutritional Support (NS). The study design is a randomized controlled trial with 2 treatment arms and 3 assessment points (pre, post, and follow-up) using questionnaire data and clinical interviews.

interventions.name: Supportive Parenting for Anxious Childhood Emotions (SPACE)

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Be between 6 and 12 years old.
* Meet DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for ARFID, as determined by the PARDI diagnostic interview.
* Cease all other psychotherapeutic treatment targeting eating or feeding behaviors, upon consultation with project staff and the current service provider.
* Not currently use any psychotropic medication, unless on a stable dose for a minimum of 4 weeks prior to enrollment; no changes anticipated during the course of the study.
* BMI at or above the 5th percentile for age and sex.
* Have an eligible and willing participating parent (see parent exclusions below).

Exclusion Criteria:

Adolescents:

* Meet criteria for any other DSM-5 disorder as determined by the ADIS diagnostic interview and health history form, that is sufficiently impairing or disruptive so as to make treatment focused on ARFID not feasible.
* Have any of the following disorders: intellectual disability; bipolar disorder; schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders; and alcohol and substance use disorders, as determined by the health history form.
* Report a suicide attempt in the last 3 months, or current suicide intent and/or plans.
* Be a victim of past or present undisclosed abuse requiring investigation or ongoing supervision by the Department of Children and Families.
* Not have sufficient proficiency in English to complete assessments.
* Require a level of medical care for nutritional compromise that exceeds what can be safely provided in an outpatient setting.

Parents:

* Have any of the following: intellectual disability; untreated bipolar disorder; untreated schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders; and untreated alcohol and substance use disorders, report a suicide attempt in the last 3 months, or current suicide intent and/or plans.
* Not be living with the child at least 50% of the time.
* Not have sufficient proficiency in English to complete assessments and participate in treatment.
